meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'me', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not look at me like that.
You must not be overfed right now.
I am inspecting your restaurant.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'only', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Just do not worry.
Brother, just do not worry!
Yes, just do not tell anyone.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What kind of total nonsense is this?
Now we will think of something, Chef.
Timur, what have you done here?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'zipper; lightning' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Lightning just struck me.
Zipper down, down!
Zip up the zipper.

meanings.en: to hit, to strike, to punch
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'дарить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to hit, to strike', paired with 'ударять'.

examples.trans: Then why did you hit me?
Lightning just struck me.
Well, come on, hit me!

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'forgive', paired with 'прощать'.

examples.trans: Lena, forgive me for everything.
Forgive me for hiding it from you.
Vitya, forgive me, please.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It overshadowed that unpleasant incident.
Thank you for the kind words.
What kind of total nonsense is this?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Is everything alright with you?
We will wash everything out quickly.
We will fix everything!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You will not withstand a blow from a coconut.
Why did you do that just now?
How foolish you are!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello, I am very pleased to meet you.
This is simply very outrageous!
I love you very much.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ильно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I did not hit him very hard.
The hotel guests are complaining about loud noise.
I love you very much.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'like', paired with 'полюбить'.

examples.trans: I always loved him deeply.
I love our town very much.
Do you like gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello, Viktor Petrovich.
I am inspecting your restaurant.
Hello, I am very pleased to meet you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'happened', paired with 'случаться'.

examples.trans: What happened?
Nothing will happen.

examples.text: Марина, я вам обещаю: со стеной ничего не случится.
examples.trans: Marina, I promise you: nothing will happen to the wall.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пасть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'got in', paired with 'попадать'.

examples.trans: A firework hit the power station.
How do I get to the station?

examples.text: Скажи: салют попал в станцию. Три района без света.
examples.trans: Say a firework hit the power station. Three districts without electricity.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello, Viktor Petrovich.
I am inspecting your restaurant.
Is everything alright with you?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big').

examples.trans: We need big money.
And there came to be even more money.
That is just from great pleasure.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'trouble' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I got into big trouble.
That's no big deal.

examples.text: Ну, допустим, я жулик. А ты жадина и не помогаешь людям в беде.
examples.trans: All right, let's say I'm a crook. But you're greedy, and you don't help people in trouble.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'because of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Because of me a person died today.

examples.text: Из-за вашей Лёли весь класс зовёт меня врунишкой!
examples.trans: Because of your Lyolya the whole class calls me a little liar!
We were late because of the rain.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.trans: Nobody is going to die here today!
Today I am covering for you here.
Chef, are you going to win it back today?

meanings.en: to die, to perish, to be killed (in an accident or disaster)
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'гибнуть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'died / perished', paired with 'погибать'.

examples.text: Ты же говорила, что он погиб!
examples.trans: You said that he died!
His grandfather died in the war.

examples.text: Что?! Это твой отец? Ты же говорила, что он погиб!
examples.trans: What?! That's your father? You said that he died!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'man' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Fedya, escort the man, please.
Because of me a person died today.
A human would not have been able to work.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will arrive', paired with 'приезжать'.

examples.trans: Which car did you come in?
Pasha has arrived.

examples.text: Вика, ты на какой машине сегодня приехала?
examples.trans: Vika, which car did you come in today?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We will wash everything out quickly.
We will fix everything!
We do not wish you any harm.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will sort out, will solve', paired with 'решать'.

examples.trans: I will come over, we will solve everything.
The court has decided.
I've decided.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'крывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hide; to conceal', paired with 'скрыть'.

examples.trans: Forgive me for hiding it from you.

examples.text: Зачем ты скрывал правду от своей жены?
examples.trans: Why did you hide the truth from your wife?

examples.text: Ты явно скрываешь от меня правду.
examples.trans: You are clearly concealing the truth from me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not look at me like that.
Your signature set is simply excellent.
It overshadowed that unpleasant incident.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'India' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: В Индии я была по заданию.
examples.trans: In India I was on an assignment.
He arrived from India.

examples.text: Они привели нового шеф-повара прямо из Индии.
examples.trans: They brought a new chef straight from India.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'was'.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'according to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Is everything alright with you?
What kind of total nonsense is this?
So will I get this star?

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'дание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'mission, assignment, task' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: В Индии я была по заданию.
examples.trans: In India I was on an assignment.

examples.text: Вы не знаете, что мы на задании?
examples.trans: Don't you know that we're on a mission?
This is a secret mission.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: I am inspecting your restaurant.
For the sake of the restaurant I grudge nothing.
The restaurant was only my cover.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello, did my husband stop by here?
After all, I live with my mother.
Denis, thank you, you are my savior!

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'крытие'). Common neuter noun meaning 'cover' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The restaurant was only my cover.
Was that also your cover story?

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must, ought to').

examples.trans: I must see your review.
I have to watch over you.
You must leave the country urgently.

следить.gloss: to watch, to follow; to keep an eye on

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ледить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to watch, to follow; to keep an eye on', paired with 'проследить'.

examples.trans: We need to quietly keep an eye on her.
Go with him and keep watch.
I have to watch over you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'стоянно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I constantly cleaned up after you.
What are you constantly afraid of?
He was constantly late for work.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'чищать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'cleaned up after'.

related.gloss: not to cleaned up after (negated infinitive)

examples.trans: I constantly cleaned up after you.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и подчищать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and cleaned up after on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It overshadowed that unpleasant incident.
What kind of total nonsense is this?
Chef, those were just coconuts.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: A coconut has already fallen on me.
The money is already with us.
We are already running out of vases.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'следний'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('last').

examples.trans: This is already the last time.
First and last time.
This is my last question.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'time, occasion' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is just a foolish misunderstanding.
She will call the police right away.
Enough, let us sort this out calmly.
